statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-47242 (GHSA-46q3-7gv7-qmgg): Net::IMAP#id and Net::IMAP#enable do not validate their arguments, so caller-supplied input containing CRLF can inject further IMAP commands. The GitHub advisory lists net-imap 0.5.15 and 0.6.4.1 as the fixed releases: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/security/advisories/GHSA-46q3-7gv7-qmgg. It lists no 0.4 release, but the net-imap 0.4.25 release notes name this CVE, so on the 0.4 release line it is fixed in net-imap 0.4.25: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/releases/tag/v0.4.25. In the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, net-imap ships in the ruby3.3-net-imap package, which is built from the ruby-3.3 source with its own version number; ruby-3.3-full depends on it. We downloaded every published ruby3.3-net-imap package for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64, checked each against its repository index checksum, and compared its installed lib directory with the net-imap release from rubygems.org; each matches its release byte for byte: 0.4.21-r0, 0.4.21-r1 and 0.4.21-r2 install net-imap 0.4.21, 0.4.21-r3 installs net-imap 0.4.24, and 0.4.25-r3 and 0.4.25-r4 install net-imap 0.4.25. Each ruby-3.3 build is built together with the ruby3.3-net-imap package of the same package release (-rN): 3.3.10-r0 to 3.3.11-r2 with net-imap 0.4.21 (ruby3.3-net-imap 0.4.21-r0 to 0.4.21-r2); 3.3.11-r3, which upgrades the bundled net-imap to 0.4.24, with ruby3.3-net-imap 0.4.21-r3; and 3.3.12-r3, 3.3.13-r3, 3.3.14-r3 and 3.3.14-r4, whose Ruby releases bundle net-imap 0.4.25, with ruby3.3-net-imap 0.4.25-r3 and 0.4.25-r4. The published DHI Ruby 3.3.11 and 3.3.12 dev images for Alpine 3.23 install ruby-3.3 3.3.11-r3 with ruby3.3-net-imap 0.4.21-r3 (net-imap 0.4.24) and ruby-3.3 3.3.12-r3 with ruby3.3-net-imap 0.4.25-r3 (net-imap 0.4.25), on amd64 and arm64. The ruby-3.3-libs 3.3.11-r3 package also carries the net-imap 0.4.24 gem archive, identical to the rubygems.org file; ruby-3.3-libs 3.3.11-r2 carries none. So the first published ruby-3.3 build that ships the fix is 3.3.12-r3: the builds before it ship net-imap 0.4.21 or 0.4.24, and it and every later build ship net-imap 0.4.25.

CVE-2026-47242 (GHSA-46q3-7gv7-qmgg): in the Ruby net-imap gem, Net::IMAP#id does not reject CR or LF in the values of its hash argument, and Net::IMAP#enable sends its arguments without checking that they are valid atoms, so an application that passes untrusted input to either command can be made to send additional IMAP commands (command injection): https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/security/advisories/GHSA-46q3-7gv7-qmgg. Upstream fixed it in net-imap 0.4.25 on the 0.4 line, 0.5.15 on the 0.5 line and 0.6.4.1 on the 0.6 line; the 0.5.15 release notes list CVE-2026-47242: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/releases/tag/v0.5.15. The DHI ruby-3.4 package for Alpine 3.23 is published as 3.4.8-r0, 3.4.8-r1, 3.4.9-r1, 3.4.9-r2, 3.4.10-r2, 3.4.10-r3, 3.4.11-r3, 3.4.12-r3, 3.4.13-r3 and 3.4.13-r4, for x86_64 and aarch64. It ships net-imap in its ruby3.4-net-imap gem package, which carries the gem's version rather than Ruby's, so the range below is written in the ruby-3.4 package's own versions, and each ruby-3.4 build is placed by the net-imap its ruby3.4-net-imap package installs. The gem package keeps the gem's own version but takes its -rN release number from the Ruby build that produced it, and the repository keeps one copy of each package version, so the gem package versions published under a given -rN are exactly the net-imap releases the Ruby builds with that -rN shipped. We read Net::IMAP::VERSION in lib/net/imap.rb of every published ruby3.4-net-imap package for both architectures, each verified against the repository index checksum, and listed the contents of every published ruby-3.4-libs package: the published ruby3.4-net-imap packages are 0.5.8-r0, 0.5.8-r1, 0.5.8-r2, 0.5.15-r2, 0.5.15-r3 and 0.5.15-r4. 0.5.8-r0 and 0.5.8-r1 install net-imap 0.5.8, which Ruby 3.4.8 and 3.4.9 bundle, per https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/v3_4_9/gems/bundled_gems, so 3.4.8-r0, 3.4.8-r1 and 3.4.9-r1 ship 0.5.8. Under -r2 two gem versions exist: 0.5.8-r2, which despite its label installs net-imap 0.5.14 (ruby-3.4-libs 3.4.9-r2 still carries the net-imap-0.5.14 gem archive that install left behind, and no other ruby-3.4-libs build carries a net-imap archive), and 0.5.15-r2, which installs net-imap 0.5.15. Ruby 3.4.10 onward bundles net-imap 0.5.15, per https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/v3_4_10/gems/bundled_gems, so 3.4.9-r2 is the build that replaced its bundled 0.5.8 with 0.5.14, and 3.4.10-r2 ships the bundled 0.5.15. 0.5.15-r3 and 0.5.15-r4 install net-imap 0.5.15, so 3.4.10-r3, 3.4.11-r3, 3.4.12-r3, 3.4.13-r3 and 3.4.13-r4 ship 0.5.15. Both architectures agree for every build. Every ruby-3.4 build before 3.4.10-r2 ships a net-imap without this fix, and 3.4.10-r2 is the first that ships net-imap 0.5.15, so the range is introduced at the first published build and fixed at 3.4.10-r2.

CVE-2026-47242 (GHSA-46q3-7gv7-qmgg): in the Ruby net-imap gem before 0.6.4.1 on the 0.6 release line (and before 0.5.15), Net::IMAP#id does not reject CR or LF in the ID field values it quotes, and Net::IMAP#enable sends its arguments verbatim without checking that they are atoms, so an application that passes untrusted input to either command can be made to send additional IMAP commands: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/security/advisories/GHSA-46q3-7gv7-qmgg. It is fixed in net-imap 0.6.4.1 (https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/releases/tag/v0.6.4.1) by https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/pull/698 (commit https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/commit/8d9397abeafc, which makes the quoted strings #id sends go through the same CR, LF and NULL validation as other text arguments via a new ValidNonLiteralData class in lib/net/imap/command_data.rb) and https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/pull/699 (commit https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/commit/1f97168be633, which sends each #enable argument as a validated atom); neither change is in v0.6.4. Ruby 4.0.1 to 4.0.5 bundle net-imap 0.6.2 and Ruby 4.0.6 and later bundle 0.6.4.1, per gems/bundled_gems at those tags. The DHI ruby-4.0 package for Alpine 3.23 is published, as of 2026-11-28, as 4.0.1-r0, 4.0.1-r1, 4.0.2-r1, 4.0.2-r2, 4.0.3-r2, 4.0.4-r2, 4.0.4-r3, 4.0.5-r3, 4.0.6-r3, 4.0.6-r4, 4.0.7-r4, 4.0.9-r4, 4.0.10-r4 and 4.0.10-r5, for x86_64 and aarch64. We downloaded all 654 packages built from the ruby-4.0 source for Alpine 3.23, each checked against the repository index checksum (the interpreter packages ruby-4.0, ruby-4.0-libs, ruby-4.0-dev, ruby-4.0-doc, ruby-4.0-dbg and ruby-4.0-full for every build, and 40 gem packages, ruby4.0-abbrev to ruby4.0-typeprof, which carry the gem's version rather than Ruby's), listed every file in them and opened the net-imap gem archives among them. net-imap is installed only by the ruby4.0-net-imap package; the only other copies are net-imap-0.6.4.gem archives left in the gem cache of ruby-4.0-libs 4.0.4-r3 and 4.0.5-r3. The published ruby4.0-net-imap packages are 0.6.2-r0, 0.6.2-r1 and 0.6.2-r2 (net-imap 0.6.2), 0.6.2-r3 (which despite its label installs net-imap 0.6.4), and 0.6.4.1-r3, 0.6.4.1-r4 and 0.6.4.1-r5 (net-imap 0.6.4.1). The lib/net/imap/command_data.rb of net-imap 0.6.4.1 in every ruby4.0-net-imap 0.6.4.1 package contains the ValidNonLiteralData class and lib/net/imap.rb sends ENABLE arguments as separate validated atoms; the net-imap 0.6.2 and 0.6.4 copies, including the cached 0.6.4 gems, contain neither. Every build before 4.0.6-r3 ships a net-imap without this fix, including the net-imap 0.6.2 and 0.6.4 this request matched, so the range starts at the first published build and ends at 4.0.6-r3, the first build that ships net-imap 0.6.4.1.
